verdicts.feedback: 1. BUG: EnterWithRangeStop sets SetStopLoss BEFORE SetProfitTarget, but requirement §16/Q1 mandates target-first tie-break — SetProfitTarget must come first. 2. BUG: RangeSizeFilter uses BarsArray[0].GetClose(1) which returns the previous intraday bar's close, not the prior day's close. For an intraday strategy this gives the wrong reference price. Should use prior session/day close. 3. MISSING: ADR-002 requires MAE/MFE logged as price % (mae/rangeMid*100) — no such logging exists anywhere in the class. 4. Minor: ToET treats Unspecified as Central Time unconditionally; if Time[0] Kind is already Unspecified but represents a different zone, conversion is wrong. Acceptable for CME futures context but fragile.

Violations: (1) ADR-001 — ToET() treats DateTimeKind.Unspecified as Central Time (exchange-local) per an inline comment, but ADR-001 mandates that charts provide UTC-naive inputs; Unspecified must be promoted to UTC then converted to ET. Local also incorrectly round-trips through Chicago. (2) Q1 same-bar tie-break — EnterWithRangeStop calls SetStopLoss BEFORE SetProfitTarget, contradicting the documented 'target-first' rule (Q1). The inline comment even claims 'SetProfitTarget before SetStopLoss' but the code does the opposite. (3) ADR-002 design gap — No MAE/MFE logging hook exists; per requirement #15 the base must expose a virtual method that logs as price% (mae/rangeMid*100), never raw points. Minor: rangeStarted is declared but never flipped to true in the base; FinalizeRange does not call SetStopLoss/SetProfitTarget order consistently with the documented Q1 rule. No ADR-017/020/021/018 violations (C# event-driven, not Python; base RiskManagerBase owns 16:00 ET flatten; no hardcoded NQ/YM symbols; 0.25R stop preserves IB 96% rationale).

- Class XML documentation present but could be more comprehensive per repo header convention
- C# naming conventions followed correctly (PascalCase methods/properties, camelCase private fields)
- Heavy #region usage acceptable for C# but consider reducing nesting
- CalendarSkipRule record syntax (C# 9+) may not be compatible with NinjaTrader 8's scripting environment - consider using class instead
- OnConnectionStatusUpdate override signature doesn't match standard NinjaTrader Strategy base class - will cause compilation error
- OnOrderUpdate parameter list should match RiskManagerBase signature exactly
- ToET/ToUTC methods are overly complex for NinjaTrader environment - simplify or use NinjaTrader's built-in Time utilities
- Some methods lack null safety checks (e.g., BarsArray[0].GetClose(1) could throw)
- Line lengths generally acceptable but some exceed 110 chars in parameter declarations
- No dead code or commented blocks detected
- Abstract method contracts clearly defined with XML docs
- Consider adding explicit interface documentation for subclass implementers
